newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - Soros investment stirs up Moulinex.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Soros investment stirs up Moulinex.

text.p: Shares in ailing appliance maker Moulinex rose on Thursday after international financier George Soros took a 5.5 percent stake, but most investors on the Paris bourse bet on Moulinex's healthier rival, SEB.
Moulinex shares initially shot up more than five percent to 117.90 francs on Soros's investment, which was announced on Wednesday evening by the French stockmarkets association SBF.

But the shares slipped from their highs to close at 112.50 francs, up 1.3 percent, as analysts said they did not believe the move signalled bid intentions. They said they viewed it more as a vote of confidence in the company's recovery plan.
Shares in SEB, which also makes household electrical appliances, surged 2.89 percent to close at 1,032 francs. "People feel it has better fundamentals," a trader said.
SEB's profit flattened in the first half of 1996 after a 13 percent rise in 1995, but Moulinex has not turned a profit in any of the past four years.
Analysts say the company, which has drifted since the death in 1988 of its founder Jean Mantelet, is hobbled by high labour costs, old and inefficient factories and a dated product line.

When chairman Pierre Blayau unveiled his restructuring plan in June, he said the objective was to bring Moulinex's operating performance up to the standards of rivals such as SEB and Gillette's Braun subsidiary.
Moulinex's stock has gained around 40 percent since the restructuring plan was announced.
The company refused to comment on Soros's move, but a source close to Moulinex said his investment, estimated at 170 million francs ($33.5 million), was not perceived as a takeover move.

He added that the shareholder structure -- a typically French cascade of holding companies -- provided some protection from unwelcome advances. Moulinex's biggest shareholder, Euris, holds 33 percent of Financiere Moulinex, which in turn controls 28 percent of Moulinex and 41 percent of the voting rights.

"But Moulinex is a globally recognised brand, Krupps (its coffee maker line) is known in Germany and the United States, and this is an industry in which the French are good," he said, citing SEB as an example. "We think Soros has made the same analysis."
Analyst Lilyane Dufroid Reynaud at brokerage SGE Delahaye said she also believed Soros viewed Moulinex as a good investment.

"Soros looks for shares with potential, and he estimates that, at that price, the stock is worth it," she said. She added that she thought the share had further scope to rise if the restructuring plan went through.

Although investors have applauded the plan, the management has drawn fire from workers and politicians for what is viewed as an extremely brutal solution by French standards. The plan entails job cuts of more than 20 percent and two plant closures.
The company's staff committee, which includes worker representatives, will examine the plan on December 6 in what promises to be a heated session.
